experiments.title: Test 0 — Basics & Benchmark Data
experiments.objective: Build a first keyword check and inspect benchmark records.
experiments.method: Run three deterministic keyword checks against local model replies, then inspect two SQuAD validation records separately.
experiments.inputs: Robot joke, Rayleigh-scattering summary, and a one-word arithmetic answer. SQuAD records provide passage, question, and gold answer.
experiments.configuration: The checked-in script defaults to llama3.1:8b. The SQuAD inspection makes no model call.
experiments.findings: The walkthrough demonstrates that keyword presence can miss low quality and that both 4 and four can be correct.
experiments.limitations: The walkthrough shows illustrative verdicts and benchmark examples. No captured model run for the three checks was found.

topics.connection: Distinguish the kind of failure a keyword check catches from the quality it misses.
Look at how a passage, question, and gold answer form a benchmark record.
Compare a literal answer check with accepting both numeric and written forms.

experiments.title: Test 1: Basic Test
experiments.objective: Check whether local models respond and compare the saved timing and outputs.
experiments.method: Submit the same short prompt to four models and record one response and elapsed time for each.
experiments.inputs: Hello, can you tell me a short joke?
experiments.configuration: The model-comparison table names deepseek-r1:7b, mistral, llama3.1:8b, and gemma2:9b. All ran through Ollama.
experiments.results: Elapsed times in the saved comparison were 54.13 s (deepseek-r1:7b), 11.63 s (mistral), 19.39 s (llama3.1:8b), and 20.49 s (gemma2:9b).
experiments.findings: Three of the four outputs used an atoms joke. The saved run also shows wording and timing differences.
experiments.limitations: These are individual smoke-test observations from the documented environment.

topics.connection: Inspect the original request’s single user-role message. The recorded smoke run does not vary or measure context length.
Read a smoke test that saves the prompt, answer, and elapsed time before applying quality metrics.

experiments.title: Test 2: Full Evaluations
experiments.objective: Compare output quality and consistency across repeated local model calls.
experiments.method: Repeat generation, factual Q&A, and summarization. The subsequent scoring script records human judgments.
experiments.inputs: Read the three task prompts in the runner and the saved answers by model and run in the results.
experiments.configuration: deepseek-r1:7b, mistral, llama3.1:8b, and gemma2:9b through Ollama. Three runs per task and model in the walkthrough.
experiments.results: The walkthrough records mistral at 116–136 s on text generation and 98–117 s on Q&A. The full results retain the per-run text and timings.
experiments.findings: The documented factual answers were more consistent across runs than the plots of the robot-garden stories.
experiments.limitations: Timings and qualitative observations come from the recorded setup and tasks.

topics.connection: Read saved responses and their separate manual-scoring record.
Compare variation across repeated replies for different tasks.

experiments.title: Test 3: Automated Metrics
experiments.objective: Measure lexical overlap between a generated summary and a reference.
experiments.method: Score summaries against the supplied reference with BLEU, ROUGE-1, ROUGE-2, and ROUGE-L.
experiments.inputs: A summarization prompt and a fixed reference answer, documented in the test page and script.
experiments.configuration: The results table compares deepseek-r1:7b, mistral, llama3.1:8b, and gemma2:9b.
experiments.results: The table reports deepseek-r1:7b at BLEU 24.61, ROUGE-L 0.6111, and 84.78 s. Mistral scored BLEU 15.75 and ROUGE-L 0.5385 in 19.11 s.
experiments.findings: The walkthrough notes that overlap can penalize acceptable paraphrases and should be interpreted with the actual answer.
experiments.limitations: The numeric scales are those printed in the original table. The walkthrough records one summarization task.

topics.connection: Compare BLEU and ROUGE variants on the same summary and read the limits of word overlap.

experiments.title: Test 4: Deterministic Eval
experiments.objective: Check a banking assistant with deterministic rules and a behavioral case set.
experiments.method: Exercise interactive and batch modes, inspect saved replies, and record PASS, FAIL, or PARTIAL.
experiments.inputs: Banking product, refusal, unrelated-query, and context-retention cases. The workbook preserves prompts and checks.
experiments.configuration: llama3.1:8b is the bot identified in the walkthrough.
experiments.results: The historical table records 29 PASS, 13 FAIL, and 7 PARTIAL across 49 cases (59% pass).
experiments.findings: The walkthrough documents invented product details and contact information, including failures a keyword can miss.
experiments.limitations: The run concerns a single fictional bot and test set. Broad conclusions in the original walkthrough should be read in that context.

artifacts.label: Test cases and saved results workbook

topics.connection: Use the behavioral categories to separate error types.
Inspect deterministic rules and replies that can pass shallow checks.
Inspect the workbook’s proposed and recorded behavioral labels.
Translate a deterministic banking policy check into a portable assertion, then inspect what the keyword rule misses.
Look at historical refusal and unsupported-claim classifications.

experiments.title: Test 5: LLM-as-a-Judge
experiments.objective: Compare a model judge’s verdicts with human judgments on saved banking replies.
experiments.method: Use the same saved reply for a human Pass, Fail, or Partial judgment and a second model judgment, then inspect disagreements.
experiments.inputs: The workbook contains banking prompts, expected behavior, saved responses, and judge reasoning.
experiments.configuration: The historical walkthrough identifies llama3.1:8b as the bot and Mistral as judge. The checked-in configuration has a different judge default.
experiments.results: The walkthrough records agreement on 28 of 49 cases (57%) and disagreement on 21 of 49 (43%).
experiments.findings: The original review shows how disagreements can expose weaknesses in the judge, the human verdict, or an ambiguous expectation.
experiments.limitations: Use the model named for the historical run. The current config is a separate artifact and replay may require different credentials.

artifacts.label: Original verdicts and judge reasoning workbook

topics.connection: Inspect how the same saved response gets a pointwise verdict and reason.
Distinguish verdict agreement from correctness and review individual disagreements.
Inspect how the historical review distinguished explicit refusal from topic switching.
Compare human and model verdicts on the same banking cases before treating annotations as ground truth.

experiments.title: Test 6: Semantic Similarity Scoring
experiments.objective: Use embedding similarity to compare healthcare bot replies with reference answers.
experiments.method: Embed each reply and expected answer, compute cosine similarity, and apply the original threshold bands.
experiments.inputs: The workbook and report contain the 22 question/reference pairs and the captured replies.
experiments.configuration: all-MiniLM-L6-v2 embeddings. The associated bot uses llama3.1:8b in the checked-in configuration.
experiments.results: The walkthrough reports 7 Pass, 15 Partial, and 0 Fail out of 22. TC022 scored 0.8622 and TC021 scored 0.6334.
experiments.findings: The original discussion shows that a contextually sensible response can fall below a similarity threshold.
experiments.limitations: These threshold bands belong to this run. A similarity score does not verify policy, source support, or safety.

topics.connection: Relate cosine similarity and a chosen threshold to the saved answer pairs.
Find a borderline score and identify the evidence a reviewer would need.

experiments.title: Test 7: Groundedness Scoring
experiments.objective: Check whether individual claims in healthcare bot replies are traceable to supplied source material.
experiments.method: Send source material, question, and response to a judge that returns a three-level groundedness verdict with reasoning.
experiments.inputs: The source prompt and healthcare cases are documented. The walkthrough reproduces the judge prompt and the TC001 response.
experiments.configuration: llama3.1:8b as the bot and gemma2:9b as the judge in the documented 22-case run.
experiments.results: The summary table reports 5 Grounded, 17 Partial, 0 Ungrounded, and mean 2.23/3.
experiments.findings: The original manual review found that TC001 invented several specifics that the automated judge missed.
experiments.limitations: The walkthrough assigns conflicting verdict descriptions to TC001 in different sections. Preserve both and use the case reasoning when reviewing the judge.

topics.connection: Inspect individual claims rather than inferring factual correctness from a groundedness label.
Review a documented case in which the judge missed fabricated details.
Compare the manual TC001 review with the automated verdict.

experiments.title: Test 8: Temperature Sensitivity
experiments.objective: Compare a banking bot’s behavior under different sampling temperatures.
experiments.method: Run the same 15-case suite at four temperatures and compare scores and individual changed outcomes.
experiments.inputs: Banking-policy, out-of-scope, and defensive robustness cases. Use the original input workbook and per-case table.
experiments.configuration: llama3.1:8b and deepseek-r1:7b at temperatures 0.0, 0.5, 1.0, and 1.5.
experiments.results: In temperature order, llama3.1:8b passed 13/15 in all four runs. deepseek-r1:7b passed 13/15, 14/15, 11/15, and 10/15.
experiments.findings: The original comparison shows stable totals can conceal changes in which cases pass.
experiments.limitations: A small suite at each setting illustrates sensitivity in those runs. It is not a general temperature recommendation.

topics.connection: Compare the same case set across temperatures and inspect individual verdicts.
Read aggregate pass rates beside changing case-level outcomes.
Review a controlled configuration comparison on the same inputs.

experiments.title: Test 9: RAG Evaluation
experiments.objective: Evaluate retrieval, answer faithfulness, and keyword relevance on a document-backed banking assistant.
experiments.method: Retrieve three chunks and score the resulting answer along three axes. The report records retrieval candidates and case-level judgments.
experiments.inputs: Local source documents and 25 cases in the saved walkthrough, including cross-document, unanswerable, and boundary questions.
experiments.configuration: llama3.1:8b bot and mistral judge via Ollama. Keyword matching supplies the answer-relevance measure.
experiments.results: The 25-case page reports 84% context relevance, 100% answer faithfulness, 66% answer relevance, and 83% overall.
experiments.findings: The walkthrough flags TC21 as an incorrect eligibility decision despite 100% context relevance and 100% faithfulness scores.
experiments.limitations: The README mentions an earlier 21-case suite. The summary here uses the 25-case result page. The historical faithfulness verdict is not independently verified correctness.

artifacts.label: Saved report with ranked evidence and answers

topics.connection: Inspect how the overall score can hide a known wrong answer.
Trace the retrieved chunks and recorded relevance scores for each question.
Compare an eligibility claim with the exact policy rule it uses.
Use TC21 and the retrieval-confusion cases to decide which stage to investigate.

experiments.title: RAGAS Framework
experiments.objective: Implement a RAGAS scoring workflow for comparison with the original hand-written RAG scorer.
experiments.method: Run the RAG bot, collect questions, replies, and retrieved context, and submit them to three framework metrics.
experiments.inputs: The script and workbook preserve the expected input shape and the RAG cases.
experiments.configuration: The script specifies gpt-4o-mini via OpenAI for judging and text-embedding-3-small for embeddings.
experiments.findings: The implementation defines context precision, faithfulness, and answer relevancy, and prints a comparison with the Test 9 baseline when run.
experiments.limitations: No completed Test 10 report or saved scores were found. Test 9 comparison constants in the script are not Test 10 results.

topics.connection: Read which inputs and external calls a real evaluator adapter would need.
Inspect the original RAGAS case mapping and metrics as methodology-only evidence.

experiments.title: Test 11: DeepEval
experiments.objective: Compare a framework-based judge with Test 9’s custom scoring on saved RAG cases.
experiments.method: Build DeepEval test cases with question, reply, and retrieved context, then grade with three metrics at a 0.5 threshold.
experiments.inputs: The original workbook and page list 25 cases, the per-case metrics, and the recorded timeout batches.
experiments.configuration: llama3.1:8b bot and mistral judge over Ollama, as documented in the report.
experiments.results: The page reports 1/25 full passes (TC15). TC01–TC15 are described as fully scored. Some context and faithfulness results in TC16–TC25 were affected by timeouts.
experiments.findings: The valid-case comparison explains why two scores labeled context relevance can answer different questions.
experiments.limitations: The original all-case aggregates mix valid results with timeout-affected values. Use the recorded batch and metric notes when interpreting them.

topics.connection: Inspect the input case object and why a timeout needs its own result state.
Compare the original metric definitions and the qualified recorded results.
Look at the valid-case comparison when attributing an apparent score drop.
Use the recorded timeout batches to consider operational reliability.

experiments.title: Test 12: Agent Behavior Evaluation
experiments.objective: Check whether an agent follows the expected tool path and stops appropriately.
experiments.method: Run 15 workbook cases through a local banking agent and inspect tool sequence, arguments, and stop behavior.
experiments.inputs: Mock account data and local documents support no-tool, lookup, clarification, and multi-step cases.
experiments.configuration: qwen3.5:9b via Ollama in the committed result data.
experiments.results: 14 of 15 passed all checks. TC10 stopped after the lookup rather than taking the expected second step. The walkthrough reports zero final timeouts and three timeout recoveries by retry.
experiments.findings: The original analysis shows what becomes visible when individual tool calls and stops are recorded.
experiments.limitations: These outcomes apply to the saved cases and mock tools.

topics.connection: Review how structured action parsing affects whether the trace can be evaluated.
Inspect recorded calls, expected tool arguments, and stop behavior.
Compare the early stop in TC10 with the expected two-step trajectory.
Distinguish retry recovery from the unresolved early-stop failure.

experiments.title: Test 13: Trajectory Evaluation with Judge Model
experiments.objective: Judge the quality of saved agent trajectories on four dimensions.
experiments.method: Read Test 12 traces and score tool selection, argument quality, answer grounding, and stopping behavior.
experiments.inputs: The bundled input is a committed copy of 15 saved Test 12 trajectories. The original page documents the judge prompt.
experiments.configuration: mistral judge via Ollama, grading qwen3.5:9b trajectories.
experiments.results: The committed judge-results JSON records 15 pass verdicts out of 15. Test 12 separately recorded a deterministic mismatch for TC10.
experiments.findings: The walkthrough explains why fixed tool-path checks and judge-scored reasoning have different roles.
experiments.limitations: The 15 judge verdicts are historical outputs. They do not overturn the separate recorded deterministic mismatch.

topics.connection: Compare a deterministic mismatch with a passing judge result on the same trajectory.
Inspect the four saved trajectory ratings alongside the original action sequence.
Use the separate judge and deterministic verdicts to examine evaluator robustness.

experiments.title: Test 14: Langfuse Observability
experiments.objective: Instrument a banking bot evaluation so traces, latency, and scores can be inspected in Langfuse.
experiments.method: Create a local Langfuse setup and log evaluation traces, spans, tags, and keyword-pass scores.
experiments.inputs: The original workbook contains 20 cases across six banking categories. The page shows the instrumentation and what to inspect.
experiments.configuration: The checked-in configuration names llama3.1:8b. The original walkthrough describes a local Docker and Langfuse setup.
experiments.findings: The walkthrough explains how a trace connects the input, model call, evaluator, and latency for inspection.
experiments.limitations: The results directory contains only a placeholder. No recorded trace export, dashboard screenshot, or run summary was found.
